purpose: Restore the original first-person sense of speed and body movement in the browser.

publication.liveMultiplayerSmoke: passed: four-player race, concurrent inputs, ownership, action acknowledgments, retry, mode change and two-player co-op; 31 requests, zero retries

source.verification: UnityPy raw serialized bytes were read directly from the installed level1 and checked against recovered component field layouts.
source.eyes: The full original Main Camera and EyeAnchor matrices from the authorized car export are retained. Driver rest pitch is about11.2913 degrees; navigator rest pitch is about8.1134 degrees.

changes: Smooth speed/throttle FOV replaces fixed90-degree FOV for both occupants, bounded to90–104 degrees.
Small native-scale acceleration/braking head slide, body pitch and lateral body roll replace the almost motionless cabin.
The camera, occupants and cabin follow the same body transform and road grade, with the complete original seat rest orientation.
Original steering-wheel110-degree range follows continuous predicted steering rather than jumping at snapshot frequency.
Velocity retains directional inertia as the chassis rotates, then tyre grip settles lateral movement. Handbrake reduces lateral grip instead of preserving instantaneous direction changes.
The acceptance controller accounts for slip and brakes for peak upcoming native-road curvature. Its changes do not steer player cars.

newChecks: Bounded speed/throttle FOV and return to idle
Both real view seats use driver FOV and original eye matrices
validation.otherCoverage: Existing four-player collisions, fatal trees, tablet interactions, retry, mode selection, ownership, input expiry, stale responses and original sound tests pass.

scopeLimits: These are native serialized parameters implemented in a browser model; the native IL2CPP function bodies were not recovered by this check.
Native Unity suspension, exact tyre force model, physical roll, hand/arm IK and URP motion-blur/chromatic-aberration rendering are not reproduced by this change.
Existing browser acceleration, speed limits, camera look limits and user sensitivity controls are retained.
A fresh manual keyboard and separate-device multiplayer comparison remains necessary to judge identical feel.
